title: Find the program using a busy port and free it or pick another port
summary: The error means another program already listens on the port your program wants. Find that program with ss, then stop it or start your program on a different free port.

aliases.text: how to free a busy port
what program is using this port
Address already in use что делать

prerequisites: The port number from the error text, for example 8000
A terminal on the Linux computer

steps.explain: Show which program listens on the port. In the output, the name in quotes after users:(( is the program and pid= is its process ID. No LISTEN line means no program holds the port, so the error comes from something else.
steps.expect: A LISTEN line such as: LISTEN 0 5 0.0.0.0:8000 0.0.0.0:* users:(("python3",pid=350,fd=3))

placeholders.name: PORT
placeholders.description: The port number your program could not use, from the error line or your command

alternatives.explain: If no program name appears, the program belongs to another user or to the system. Run the same check with administrator rights.

placeholders.name: PORT
placeholders.description: The port number your program could not use

steps.explain: Stop the program that holds the port so it releases the port. Stop only a program you recognise and started yourself, never a system service. Use the pid= number from the previous output.
steps.expect: Usually no output. The program stops, and it may print a message in its own terminal window.

placeholders.name: PID
placeholders.description: Process ID number from the pid= part of the previous output

alternatives.explain: Keep the other program running and start your own program on a different free port instead. This example uses Python's built-in web server.

placeholders.name: NEW_PORT
placeholders.description: A port number that no LISTEN line uses yet

steps.explain: Check that the port is free now. If you used another port, the old port should be free too.
steps.expect: Only the header line State Recv-Q Send-Q Local Address:Port appears, with no LISTEN line.

placeholders.name: PORT
placeholders.description: The port number from the error line

steps.explain: Start your program again. It should now start without the Errno 98 error.

rollback.explain: If you stopped the wrong program, start it again the same way you started it before. Nothing else was changed.

warnings: Stopping a program ends it at once; unsaved work in that program is lost.
Use the pid= number from the same ss output. A wrong number can stop an unrelated program.
Without administrator rights, ss shows program names only for your own programs.

source.title: ss manual; card written and verified in the lnxhelp sandbox
